Queue::where¶

Back to Queue API Reference

Signature¶

static Queue where(const Queue& condition, const Queue& x, const Queue& y);

What It Does¶

A ternary conditional select: elementwise, picks x where condition is true and y where it is false. condition must hold a Series (a boolean mask); x and y must have the same kind as each other, which may be Series, Timeline, or Duration – Note is not supported.

For a Series result, this calls condition.series().where(x, y) directly. For Timeline and Duration, it forwards to x.invoke("where", {condition, y}), so the same method dispatch that backs invoke handles the actual selection.

Parameters¶

condition (const Queue&)

Must hold a Series of booleans. Any other kind is refused.

x, y (const Queue&)

The two choices, picked elementwise by condition. Must have the same kind as each other; a mismatch is refused, and Note is refused regardless of whether x and y agree.

Returns¶

A Queue of the same kind as x and y.

Errors¶

Throws when condition does not hold a Series, when x and y have different kinds, or when x/y hold Note (ternary selection on text is not supported).

Examples¶

Example 1. Selecting between two Series-holding Queues by a boolean mask.

pluss::Queue mask(pluss::make_series({true, false, true}));
pluss::Queue x(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}));
pluss::Queue y(pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0}));
pluss::Queue picked = pluss::Queue::where(mask, x, y);
std::cout << "where(mask, x, y): " << pluss::series::print(picked.series()) << '\n';

Output¶

where(mask, x, y): Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 20.0000, 3.0000]

The mask [true, false, true] picks x’s first and third elements and y’s second, matching mask ? x : y applied elementwise.

Example 2. Note is not supported, regardless of the mask.

pluss::Queue mask(pluss::make_series({true, false, true}));
pluss::Queue note_a(pluss::make_note({"a"}));
pluss::Queue note_b(pluss::make_note({"b"}));
try {
  pluss::Queue bad = pluss::Queue::where(mask, note_a, note_b);
  std::cout << "where on Note: did not throw\n";
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << "where on Note threw: " << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

where on Note threw: Queue::where failed: Queue::where: Note ternary selection is not supported
